jobs.title: Corporate Legal Counsel (Capital Markets)
jobs.description_text: Your Role In Our Mission We are seeking a highly motivated attorney with experience in structured finance / secured lending to join our legal team as Corporate Counsel. This person will play a key role in Prosper’s business, partnering closely with our Capital Markets team on a broad range of transactional matters related to our unsecured personal loan and credit card products, including institutional loan sales and servicing, credit facilities, securitizations and advising on operations, marketing and strategy related to Capital Markets. This attorney is collaborative, able to thrive in a fast-paced, complex environment, and is comfortable advising all levels of the business and management on relevant legal issues. This role will report to the Assistant General Counsel. Compensation details: The salary for this position is $193,000 - $241,000 annually, plus bonus and generous benefits. In determining your salary, we will consider your location, experience, and other job-related factors.

jobs.description_text: ABOUT YOU We are looking for a Partner Success Manager to join the Xsolla Partner Network (XPN) Business Development team, based in China. This is a newly created, hybrid role sitting within the core XPN BD team — roughly 80% campaign and partner success, 20% business development support — created to close a gap in how XPN partners are supported once a deal closes: campaigns are launched, but no one consistently owns their ongoing success. The best candidate will be someone comfortable owning outcomes rather than just relationships — proactively strategizing with partners, coordinating across internal teams to get campaigns right, and stepping in to help close deals when local presence and trust matter more than a remote pitch. Full ownership of the sales process (sourcing, pitching, commercial negotiation) sits with the Core China/APAC Team; this role isn't required to run a deal end-to-end, but is expected to help get opportunities over the line and make sure they deliver once signed. If you're excited about building a new function from the ground up, becoming a product expert partners and internal teams rely on, and working across both Chinese and global creator platforms as publishers look to expand their reach, we would love to hear from you! That's what we're building at Sona, and it's early enough that the systems you build now will still be foundational in three years. jobs.title: CENTRALE LYON - Post-doctoral researcher (12 months) Mathematics of energy-efficient AI: diffusion models on emerging hardware
jobs.description_text: The question Generating one image with a diffusion model means evaluating a large neural network tens to hundreds of times. That repetition is where the energy goes, and it is part of why data-centre demand is now visible at grid scale: the Lawrence Berkeley National Laboratory puts US data-centre electricity use at 176 TWh in 2023, 4.4 % of national consumption, a figure that more than doubled since 2017 largely because of AI servers, and projects 325–580 TWh by 2028. Emerging hardware attacks exactly this primitive: analog in-memory computing, silicon photonics, ferroelectric devices and stochastic computing perform the underlying matrix–vector products at lower energy than digital CMOS, under conditions on scale and precision, but return a perturbed result. The usual objection is that nobody can say in advance how much perturbation a model tolerates. In EMMA, this opportunity is pursued through a PCM-based photonic matrix–vector engine as the primary demonstrator, complemented where appropriate by FeFET-based analog computing, so that device-level non-idealities are treated as explicit design parameters rather than as after-the-fact implementation losses. Diffusion models are an unusual case in which that question has a mathematical answer: their convergence theory bounds the discrepancy between the generated and target distributions by three terms, of which only one, the L 2 error of the learned score, depends on the hardware.
